messages.content: 你能幫我找到紐約有閱讀室和小說區的公共圖書館，然後在洛杉磯有Wi-Fi和有兒童區的公共圖書館，最後在芝加哥有咖啡廳和閱讀室的公共圖書館嗎？

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

facilities.description: Facilities and sections in public library.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find libraries in three cities with certain facilities. We need to call the function multiple times. The function signature expects location string and facilities which can be one of the enumerated values? Wait: facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]; That means facilities can be one of those strings or an array of strings? Actually the type says union of string literal types and array of strings? It might mean you can pass either a single facility string or an array of them. But we need to provide all required ones. So for each query, we should pass an array of the needed facilities.

We need to call the function thrice:

1. For New York (NYC) with Reading Room and Fiction.
2. For Los Angeles (LA) with Wi-Fi and Children Section.
3. For Chicago with Cafe and Reading Room.

We will produce separate calls. We'll use the function name public_library_find_nearby. We'll pass location: "New York, NY", facilities: ["Reading Room","Fiction"] etc.

We'll output the results. Let's do it.
